why: Web research can surface material good enough to become a Micronaut program, and producing programs is what the factory exists for. But research output is untrusted input: a page, a hallucinated relation or a circular self-generated hypothesis must never become callable merely because the fold that carried it reached Xul. So the factory produces *proposals*, a gate audits them against the operation and capability vocabulary, and only verification plus authorization plus a shipped driver make a program callable.

pipeline.law: research -> candidates -> gate -> best proposal -> Ch'en verification -> Xul authorization -> registration
pipeline.research_phase: Yax produces evidence with provenance; evidence that was never fetched is not evidence
pipeline.factory_phase: Wo produces candidates; the factory never registers, dispatches or executes
pipeline.gate: the audit that decides whether a candidate is *admissible material* at all, before any ranking
pipeline.selection: ranking picks the best proposal; being best is a preference, not a permission

fields.operations: the program opcodes it would use
fields.capability_refs: capabilities it would expose: `cap:<token>`, a registered name, or `new:<ns>.<token>`
fields.evidence_refs: the research references that justify it
fields.declared_size: how many operations it would contain

candidate.law: a candidate is a description of a program, not a program: nothing about it is executable

audit.operations: a candidate may use only the audited opcode vocabulary the loader already enforces (ADD, MUL, CALL, LOG, CONVERT, FOLD_ENTER, FOLD_EXIT, SCO_RESOLVE, SYMBOL_RESOLVE, SET, APPEND, IMPORT, PATTERN_BANK); anything else is refused
audit.capabilities: an exposed capability must be already declared, or a namespaced `new:` token — which is then not callable until it is registered and a driver exists
audit.authority: a candidate may not declare phase, policy or commit authority: those belong to XCFE, not to a produced program
audit.size: a candidate is bounded; a runaway generated program is refused rather than truncated
audit.self_modification: a candidate may not target the factory itself unless the policy explicitly allows it
audit.evidence: every evidence reference must resolve to a fetched observation; a citation of something never retrieved is refused

ranking.score: evidence coverage x audit pass x capability reuse
ranking.coverage: min(1, sum(confidence) / 2) over the cited observations — a saturating sum, never a mean, so corroboration cannot lower the score
ranking.audit_pass: 1 for a candidate that survived every gate check, 0 for a refused one
ranking.capability_reuse: the fraction of exposed capabilities that already exist in the registry, or 0.5 for a candidate that exposes none
ranking.law: ranking orders proposals; the highest score is not an admission, and the gate's refusals are not outvoted by it

registration.law: a produced program becomes callable only when the gate admitted it, verification passed, authorization was granted, and both a driver manifest and a micronaut manifest exist
registration.why: the cfpc/xcfe defect is the precedent: a registered capability with no driver is not runnable, so production must ship the driver or the program cannot act

invariants.FR1: research evidence is untrusted input: a candidate citing an unfetched or unresolved reference is refused
invariants.FR2: the factory produces proposals only, and no path in this layer registers, dispatches or executes a program
invariants.FR3: a candidate's operations must lie within the audited opcode vocabulary; an unknown opcode is refused
invariants.FR4: an exposed capability must be already declared or a namespaced `new:` token, and a new token is not callable until registration plus a driver manifest exist
invariants.FR5: a candidate may not claim phase, policy or commit authority; authority stays with XCFE
invariants.FR6: a candidate is bounded in size, and an oversized or runaway program is refused rather than truncated
invariants.FR7: a candidate may not target the factory itself unless the policy explicitly allows self-modification
invariants.FR8: ranking is a preference: the best-scoring candidate is still a proposal, and admission requires verification plus authorization
invariants.FR9: registration requires an admitted candidate, passed verification and authorization, and both manifests — a produced program without a driver is not runnable
invariants.FR10: the gate is deterministic: the same evidence and candidates produce the same refusal or the same best proposal
